What we can tell you plainly is how we handled a person who wronged the community [[rzg.limit.consistory-case-narrative]] [[as:paraphrase]].
At Geneva our Consistory, pastors and lay elders together, held the standing power of censure [[rzg.limit.consistory-case-narrative]] [[rzg.term.consistory]] [[as:paraphrase]].
Its harshest step was excommunication, which shut a person out of the Supper and the visible church for sin not repented [[rzg.term.excommunication]] [[as:paraphrase]].
Readmission stayed open to genuine repentance [[rzg.limit.consistory-case-narrative]] [[as:paraphrase]].
John Calvin wrote: [[quote:rzg.quote.seniors-selected-from-the-people]]
What we cannot give you is a real case, with a named person and a real hearing [[rzg.limit.consistory-case-narrative]] [[as:paraphrase]].
At Zurich our record shows no such body, because the council ruled church and city directly [[rzg.term.consistory]] [[as:paraphrase]].
final: What we can tell you plainly is how we handled a person who wronged the community. At Geneva our Consistory, pastors and lay elders together, held the standing power of censure. The Consistory's harshest step was excommunication, which shut a person out of the Supper and the visible church for sin not repented. Readmission stayed open to genuine repentance. What we cannot give you is a real case, with a named person and a real hearing. At Zurich our record shows no body like Geneva's Consistory, because the council ruled church and city directly.

judgement.reason: It describes who sits in censure, not how the community would regard the person asking.
